content: Cybersecurity encompasses practices, technologies, and policies that protect digital systems, networks, and data from unauthorized access and malicious attacks. The field is guided by core principles including confidentiality (ensuring information is accessible only to authorized parties), integrity (maintaining data accuracy and trustworthiness), and availability (keeping systems operational for legitimate users). Security threats take many forms: malware includes viruses, worms, trojans, and ransomware that infiltrate systems to cause damage, steal information, or extort payments; phishing attacks use deceptive communications to trick users into revealing sensitive information or installing malware; and denial-of-service attacks overwhelm systems with traffic to render them unavailable. Defense strategies implement multiple layers (defense-in-depth) rather than relying on single protective measures. Authentication verifies user identities through factors like passwords (knowledge), security tokens (possession), or biometrics (inherence), with multi-factor authentication combining different factor types for stronger security. Authorization determines what verified users can access based on the principle of least privilegeâgiving users only the minimum access needed for their roles. Encryption protects data confidentiality by converting information into coded forms that require decryption keys to read, using symmetric algorithms for efficiency with large data or asymmetric algorithms for key exchange and digital signatures. Network security employs firewalls to control traffic based on predefined rules, intrusion detection systems to identify suspicious activities, and virtual private networks (VPNs) to create secure connections over public networks. Security operations include regular vulnerability assessments, penetration testing to identify weaknesses, patch management to update software with security fixes, and incident response plans for addressing successful attacks.

scenario.title: Privacy Protection Simulator
scenario.content: Students secure a virtual personal diary containing sensitive information, implementing multiple cybersecurity layers to protect against various threats. The simulation allows students to configure authentication systems, encryption mechanisms, access controls, backup procedures, and threat monitoring tools. The system includes simulated attackers using different techniquesâpassword cracking, social engineering, malware, and network exploitationâthat students must defend against. Students can visualize security systems in action, observing how different protective layers interact and sometimes conflict. Interactive tools let students conduct security audits, perform penetration testing, and analyze incident logs to identify vulnerabilities and attack patterns. Challenge scenarios present evolving threat landscapes that require students to adapt security measures to new attack vectors, teaching fundamental cybersecurity principles through engaging, realistic scenarios that emphasize the importance of comprehensive security thinking.

hypothesis.description: Students will implement cybersecurity systems by applying multiple protective layers to sensitive information. They will analyze how different threats exploit various vulnerabilities, and develop appropriate defense strategies that balance security, usability, and resource constraints.
